script.heading: Intro

articles.title: Pulse versus Nonpulse Corticosteroid Therapy in Acute Exacerbation of Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis: A Multicenter, Randomized Clinical Trial (SAFER).
articles.source: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
articles.summary: Acute exacerbation of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (AE-IPF) has high short-term mortality, yet guidelines weakly recommend corticosteroids without defining dose or duration. In this randomised, open-label, multicenter trial at eight South Korean university hospitals, adults with AE-IPF were assigned (1:1) to receive either intravenous pulse methylprednisolone (10 mg/kg for 3 days) or nonpulse regimen (1 mg/kg for 7 days), followed by protocolised tapering and maintenance low-dose prednisolone. Primary outcomes were all-cause mortality at 28 and 90 days. Secondary outcomes included intensive care unit admission, use of mechanical ventilation or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, death or lung transplantation at 28 and 90 days, and adverse events. From July 2021 to April 2024, 100 patients were randomised (pulse n = 51; nonpulse n = 49).
articles.analysis: Do not change practice on efficacy alone; focus journal-club discussion on whether the confidence intervals exclude a clinically important benefit or harm.

articles.title: Effect of ondansetron on respiratory drive in patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome.
articles.summary: Blocking these receptors could enable safer spontaneous ventilation and mitigate the need for deep sedation or neuromuscular blockade. We performed a single-center, single-blind, non-randomized crossover trial, including adults with ARDS (Berlin criteria), ventilated > 48 hours, on pressure-support mode. Participants underwent two consecutive phases: intravenous placebo (10 mL 0.9% saline) followed, 3 hours later, by intravenous ondansetron (0.15 mg/kg; max 16 mg). Mean inspiratory PTP fell from 108 to 85 cmH2O·s·min-1, yielding a model derived mean difference of -23 cmH2O·s·min-1 (95 % confidence interval (CI95%) [-28, -18]; p<0.001).
